title: SPC Mesoscale Discussion watch probabilities (17,119 MDs, 2012-2026) acted as three categories: 5% and 20% were followed by a watch in 0.2% and 2.4% of cases, and 60-80% were too low
abstract: Question: are the 'Probability of Watch Issuance' values (5-95%) in SPC Mesoscale Discussions (MDs) reliable, what causes any error, and do the 2025 'most probable peak' hail, gust and tornado ranges agree with storm reports? Method: a pre-registered verification of 17,119 MDs (2012-2026, IEM archive) against 9,972 SPC watch polygons (a new watch issued before MD expiry that covers >= 10% of the MD area) and 599,709 NWS Local Storm Reports, with window and overlap sensitivity tests, logistic attribution models and a 2012-2022 to 2023-2026 forward test. Results: observed watch frequencies were 0.18%, 2.4%, 31%, 73%, 90% and 94.5% for stated 5, 20, 40, 60, 80 and 95%. Thus 5% and 20% were too high by 28 and 8 times (at least 1.9 times for any window up to 6 h), and 60-80% were too low by 10-13 points. Observed log-odds rose 2.0 times as fast as stated log-odds (under-confident), with ranking AUC 0.93. MD area, time of day, region and existing watches did not explain the error. The levels follow the verbal classes 'unlikely/possible/likely', and the delay to the watch shortens with the level (median 144 to 31 min). The stated level predicted the SPC decision (AUC 0.93) far better than severe reports (AUC 0.61-0.64): 61% of 20% MDs had a severe report. An isotonic map fit on 2012-2022 improved 2023-2026 Brier skill by 0.138 (95% CI 0.117-0.159). For 2025-2026 peak hail and gust ranges, 61% and 57% of report maxima were inside the range, but for ranges above 1.50-2.50 in and 55-70 mph a lower range was the most frequent observed range. Limitations: SPC does not define the probability window; watch extensions by county are not counted; preliminary reports under-sample peak intensity and depend on population; the MP data cover under two seasons.

display.caption: Reliability of the SPC MD 'Probability of Watch Issuance' (17,119 MDs, 2012-2026). A: observed fraction of MDs followed by a new overlapping watch (>= 10% of MD area) before MD expiry (blue, day-bootstrap 95% CI), to expiry + 1 h (green) and within 6 h (orange). B: the primary result on log10-odds axes; dashed line = perfect reliability.

A: by stated level, the fraction of MDs with >= 1 and >= 6 severe Local Storm Reports in the MD area (issue to expiry + 1 h), and the fraction with a new watch. B: the severe-report fraction for MDs with and without a watch.

2025-2026 'most probable peak' ranges (shaded) against the maximum reported hail size (A, MDs with >= 1 hail report) and the maximum measured gust (B, MDs with >= 1 measured gust). Orange bar = median. Reports under-sample peak intensity.
